To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
country risk ratings and stock market returns have a nonlinear relationship in the BRICS countries.

(1) country-specific political, economic, and financial risk ratings are important determinants of stock market returns in the BRICS countries; (2) positive and negative rating changes have differential impacts on stock market returns in some BRICS nations; (3) the impact of country-specific rating changes on stock market returns is asymmetric; (4) stock returns in the BRIC countries are driven by global market factors; and (5) commodity prices have a long-run impact on stock returns in the B
country risk ratings have significant implications on stock returns and commodity price dynamics for some, but not all, BRICS countries.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BRICS countries exhibit a degree of heterogenous reaction to country-specific and global market variables.
the BRICS countries are not a homogeneous group, and that the effects of country risk ratings on their stock markets vary across countries and over time, as well as with the sign of rating changes.
the stock markets in BRICS countries are not homogeneous and their responses are asymmetric and nonlinear to country risk ratings changes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

country risk ratings and global market variables have a significant impact on BRICS stock market returns, but the impact of the country risk ratings is asymmetric, and it is greater in magnitude for negative shocks.
the stock market dynamics of BRICS countries are driven by a combination of domestic and international factors.
BRICS countries have different reactions to country risk ratings and that the impact of country risk rating changes on stock returns is asymmetric.
The main takeaway from our work is that

investors and policy makers need to be aware of the asymmetric effects that ratings changes have on emerging markets, as well as the role of international variables in the transmission of shocks to these markets.
the BRICS countries should pay more attention to their country risk ratings and their impact on the stock market returns, in addition to other factors such as commodity prices.
country-specific political, economic, and financial risks are important in understanding how these stock markets react to global shocks.
